name: WEAVER
summary: WEAVER is a multi-view world model trained with a flow-matching loss to predict both future latents and reward, built against three requirements its authors argue prior world models never satisfied simultaneously: fidelity to real physics, consistency across long rollouts, and inference fast enough for control. It is evaluated on all three uses. As an evaluator its predicted success correlates with real-world success at rho = 0.870, so it can rank policies without robot time. As a trainer it lifts real-world success by 38% on top of the pi-0.5 foundation model. As a planner it adds 14% at test time while running 5-10x faster than prior world models.
innovation: Predicts reward alongside latents, which is what turns a world model into a usable policy evaluator.
Multi-view latent rollouts consistent enough to stay useful over long horizons.
Fast enough that test-time planning is practical rather than a paper result.
matters: Real-robot evaluation is the field's bottleneck; a world model correlating at 0.870 with real success is a credible way to buy some of it back cheaply.
Improving pi-0.5 by 38% shows world models paying off as training machinery, not just as demos of video prediction.
limits: Correlation is measured over the policies and tasks tested and need not hold for very different ones.
Still a learned simulator: a policy tuned against it can learn to exploit its errors.
lineage: DreamerV3's latent-plus-reward prediction, rebuilt multi-view with flow matching and made fast enough to use.
